newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Genocide trial adjourned as Rwandan accused sick.
newsitem.headline: Genocide trial adjourned as Rwandan accused sick.

text.p: The U.N. tribunal trial of a former Rwandan Hutu mayor accused of genocide and crimes against humanity was adjourned on Wednesday after he complained of a headache.
Presiding Judge Laity Kama of Senegal adjourned until Thursday the trial of Jean-Paul Akayesu, 43, to allow a doctor to examine the accused.
"The court will be adjourned to allow the doctor to take some tests for malaria so as to establish whether his headache is caused by malaria," Kama told the court.
Kama delayed the session to allow a doctor to attend to Akayesu, who held his head and was clutching his ears and face as he sat behind a glass screen in the defendant's booth.

Akayesu has pleaded not guilty to charges of genocide and crimes against humanity involving massacres at Taba commune in central Rwanda where he was mayor in 1994 during the three- month mass slaughter.
He is the first suspect to be tried before the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and if convicted will face life imprisonment, the court's highest penalty.
Earlier Akayesu's lawyer Nicolas Tiangaye of the Central African Republic cross-examined the prosecution's 15th witness, the former mayor of a commune neighbouring on Taba.

The witness, known as "R" to protect his identity, said on April 18, 1994 he attended a meeting for commune leaders with officials from Rwanda's interrim government and was told to cooperate with the massacres.
Previous witnesses have said Akayesu also attended the meeting and began directing the killing of Tutsis immediately afterwards on April 19.
An estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus were slaughtered in Rwanda mostly by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs after the killing of Hutu president Juvenal Habyarimana.
The trial enters its third week on Thursday if Akayesu recovers and the defence will continue cross-examining witness "R", Kama said.
